correctness.rationale: Both certificate scripts were re-executed from inputs and exit 0: lower gives certified I(mu)<=1.507166683 < 1.509592577<=-ln(0.221) so cap>=0.2215368; upper gives certified min_E U>=1.473049700 > 1.469675970>=-ln(0.230) so cap<=0.2292253. Potential-theory steps match Ransford Thms 5.1.2/5.5.9. Closed forms phi(u) and F(t) verified independently against quadrature (agree to ~1e-8 off-diagonal). Upper paired enclosure is sound: h'(s)=ln|s|-ln|s+l| vanishes only at s=-l/2 with singularities only at {-l,0}, so splitting there makes each piece monotone and endpoint evaluation with certified atanh-series Fraction log bounds is a valid lower bound. Probes (40 subdivisions per interval refined at cell endpoints) cover E_3.

originality.rationale: Fused three-form search found no prior record of a certified enclosure of cap(E_3) or the interval [0.221,0.230]. Nearest results are substantively different: Ransford-Rostand (2007) estimates the infinite limit Cantor set (~0.2209), not the E_3 prefractal; Liesen-Nasser-Sete (2022/2023) gives non-rigorous CSM approximations with extrapolation, not a certified E_3 bound; Dubinin-Karp (2009/2011) gives general multi-interval bound formulas whose instantiation for E_3 is not computed or recorded. No table, database, census, or dual/transfinite-diameter formulation covers the claim.
